xratu 2.4.3 — a second engine, and a work surface that keeps up.

**OpenCode 2 is now an engine, not a wire.** Xratu can run OpenCode 2 through
its local CLI and SDK, including its public free models, so using it no longer
requires a direct Zen API connection. The Xratu engine remains for BYOK,
ChatGPT subscriptions, and local runtimes. Engines gets CLI detection and a
managed, checksum-verified installer covering Windows, macOS, and Linux on
x64, arm64, baseline x64, and musl, with **Update engine** and a confirmed
**Remove engine**. Native sessions persist their engine, workspace, binary,
and native session ID, so resuming uses that identity rather than whichever
engine happens to be selected today. First-run setup now offers free,
provider, or local paths; switching engines later starts a fresh chat.

**Free means free, and it is checked that way.** A model is classified free
only when a known public route advertises zero cost in every tier, caches
included; paid and subscription-backed routes are never probed. Availability
checks run in isolated temporary sessions, in parallel, with manual retries,
and variants use their advertised IDs. OpenCode owns its credentials and
history: your Xratu provider keys are never copied into it.

**Native subagents are coordinated, not just watched.** Delegation used to be
disabled because Xratu only observed the root session. Children now bind
through SDK-confirmed ancestry and parent native call IDs, so they can appear
live on the Agents surface, approvals and questions carry their source, and
child prose stays out of the parent ledger while usage is still accounted for.
Stop keeps the whole tree in view: it discovers missed descendants through the
native API, drains queued input, and restarts the managed process if
settlement fails. Plan still denies delegation, and with YOLO off a native
child's mutations still reach real approval cards.

**You can stop one agent without stopping the turn.** The Agents surface now
has a per-agent stop for both engines. It cancels that delegation only —
through its in-flight tools, native descendants, and background work — while
the parent turn and sibling agents keep running. Stopped runs settle as
cancelled instead of surfacing a runtime error, and turning YOLO on or off
mid-flight applies to the whole live native tree.

**Xratu's services stay Xratu's in OpenCode.** MCP servers, the marketplace,
skills, and agent files keep their normal management pages in OpenCode scope,
with native inventories shown separately and read-only. The browser, task
list, plan handoff, and enabled skills bridge into native turns, and plan mode
admits only the explicitly allowlisted read/application services. The optional
Iranian marketplace entries for Digikala, Torob, and Divar remain opt-in, and
still require a deliberate choice before anything connects or runs local code.

**Agents own their pull requests.** Six PR tools let an agent link every pull
request it works on, watch it instead of polling, and stop watching when it
hands back. Links, watch cursors, and pending updates are stored apart from the
transcripts; a check failure, review, comment, or conflict resumes the owning
idle conversation only when its workspace, branch, engine, model, and account
still match. Subagents can read PR state but cannot own a link or a watch.
Linked PRs get a sidebar and shared status in chat and Activity.

**Familiar tabs, calmer panels.** The work surface now has standard tab
controls: `+` opens a panel picker, `...` acts on the selected tab, and hover
close, middle-click, and Delete close views without stopping running work.
Overflowing strips scroll by arrows, wheel, and RTL-aware keyboard movement.
Every panel explains its empty state; Activity gets search and filters;
Conversation gains Minimal/Balanced/Detailed display levels and folds
completed steps while keeping Activity as the full trace. Restore sits where
you look for it — the message footer and the review head — and OpenCode's
files-only restore says so. Project rules now refresh each turn instead of
needing a new chat, and Changes retains review history per checkpoint.

**More text, less chrome.** Chat and composer text move to 16px with room
between messages, and a shared type scale and UI font now run across settings,
providers, engines, onboarding, and panels; code keeps the editor font. The
composer context meter is off on fresh installs and can be restored from
Settings → Conversation, and token counts leave the assistant message footers.
Usage totals now follow the selected period and filters, with free/local token
reporting, clearer pricing, and lifetime totals.

**Fixes you will feel.** Proxy-aware environments no longer break OpenCode:
authenticated localhost SDK and SSE traffic gets a direct transport and keeps
its loopback bypass, with the runtime pinned to OpenCode 2.0.30 and
checksum-verified. Native file edits stop retrying the same failing call.
Cancellation and stream failures settle cards, queued input, and sessions
without racing a reply, checkpoint restores are session-safe, and session and
workspace actions are transactional. Middle-clicking a tab on Windows is no
longer swallowed by native autoscroll, and file paths render as plain text
instead of text-code chips.

Version 2.1.0 → 2.4.3. As always: BYOK, everything local, and your credentials
never leave VS Code's secret storage.
